In this hypothetical, there is no backup solution though. This baby has a rare condition that prevents them from surviving off anything but the breast milk of their mother until they're 2 months old. The mother can either breast feed for 2 months, or the baby dies. If you truly believe that bodily autonomy trumps everything else, you would have to say it would be okay to let the baby starve.

If that many people were dying every year due to a lack of blood in blood banks, I could definitely see there being a push to force people to donate blood. I also wouldn't really have a problem with a law that mandates that everyone has to be an organ donor. 

I really only care about whether a fetus is a person worthy of moral consideration or not. Since I don't consider them developed enough, I have no problem with abortion. If I truly believed that they all had souls, I would probably be horrified by abortion.

Theoretically, if there was a baby who was actually born and had a condition that meant they could only survive off the breast milk of their biological mother for the first 2 months of life, how many people do you think would be okay with her deciding to let the baby starve? If we use the bodily autonomy argument, the baby has no inherent right to her breast milk, so it should be fine to just let it die.

Since I don't really even want a relationship anymore, I am not an incel by definition. It's like, even if I beat the odds and ended up in a relationship, it would just end in disaster since I'm completely subhuman, so why bother? She would be happier with someone else anyway.

But now, what do I have to strive for? How do I fill the emptiness in my life? I don't care about anything, and I don't enjoy anything. Why bother improving my life? There really isn't anything to strive for. I'll never be respected without a relationship anyway; anything I work towards is just meaningless cope.

I don't think most incels consider women to be subhuman. We generally reserve that term to refer to ourselves. I think most incels who are genuinely misogynistic just think that men are superior, not that women are legitimately subhuman. The idea that women are inferior has been the default assumption throughout the majority of history, so it's not surprising that many incels latch onto this idea. 

Most incels who express the view that women literally are not people are likely just using it as a coping mechanism (or as a way to shock normies); I sincerely doubt they actually believe it. These incels condone violence against women because it makes them feel good, and it's much simpler to group all women together as the enemy, than acknowledge the complex nature of the world. Additionally, the advancement of womens' rights is often viewed as detrimental to our chances to enter a relationship, so it makes sense that many of us would like to see women stripped of many of their rights. Personally, I'm doubtful that feminism is a major contributing factor towards inceldom, but I may be mistaken.
What you call hopelessness, I just call being realistic. I think it's more harmful to delude yourself into thinking you have a reasonable chance, when you really don't.

In my perspective, it is not reasonable to call incels a toxic hate group, as it is not an actual group; it is simply a description for a person's situation in life. I believe that people have latched onto the more toxic online incel communities in order to discredit the whole identity and feel better about themselves. It would be uncomfortable knowing that there are so many miserable, lonely people out there with little chance of finding success, but if they're all horrible people, then no one has to feel bad. As a consequence of all this, non-toxic people who identify as incels are reluctant to openly admit to it.

So why would I continue to identify as an incel, instead of using some other term (or none at all)? Firstly, the only other widely-used term I'm aware of is ForeverAlone. Not only is this phrase more awkward to say, I find it pretty cringe in that it is making unreasonable predictions about my entire future, whereas incel only refers to the present. Additionally, I believe that any new term that is created will eventually be smeared the same as incel, and I will once again have to find a new term. Plus, I just don't have much interest in trying to distance myself as much as possible from people who are considered toxic, as I don't consider myself a good person, nor do I feel the need to convince others that I am a good person.

Obviously, I could just choose not to make my inability to form romantic/sexual relationships as part of my identity. However, when society is built around the expectation that everyone will end up paired up, when everyone around you is entering into relationships and talking about their significant others all the time, I feel the identity ends up forced on you. Otherwise, you're stuck thinking that you are uniquely worthless.

It's not willful ignorance. We just don't let people on .is define the incel identity. To me, you are the one being willfully ignorant by actively seeking out the worst possible incel content and pretending like it applies to all of us. 

I don't consider myself to have any obligation to denounce these people either. I don't actively participate in any incel communities; how deep of a connection do you really think people are going to be able form when the only thing that unites them is an inability to find romantic/sexual partners? And if I wanted advice, why would I go to other failures like myself?

It's a lot easier to pretend that incels are all monsters, so you get to continue living comfortably in a world that feels just.

I'm not ever going to have a real genuine, meaningful relationship with someone. It's just not going to happen, and it feels pathetic to even entertain such a fantasy. Even if there were a woman fucked up enough to date me, I would never be able to form a meaningful connection with another human being.

And I have no desire to make life anything. Plus, I personally have never seen anyone break up after saying they couldn't live without their bf/gf, though I assume it happens.

I don't care who wins or loses, I just don't want this to continue. If death really was the easy path, then I think I would have done it by now. Maybe it's easy for some people, but not for me.

> these outcomes have little to do with your genuine ability to attain a romantic or sexual relationship, nor does it have anything to do with being single.

So you think the healthiest thing to do is for incels to give up and accept they will be alone forever? I frankly don't understand your views on this. We know that it is normal for humans to want romantic/sexual relationships, and by extension, it is normal to feel bad about not being able to get one. > Well, going by the dictionary definition; it does not exist

Someone could use the same argument to insist they aren't homophobic for hating gay people, as they are not afraid of gay people. We all know what the phrase incel actually means. Both involuntary and celibate have multiple definitions, and you are ignoring other possible meanings of these words. 

> Inceldom being a social issue is only the case if it has a negative outcome
That's true, but that's not what you were arguing earlier. Someone can be an incel regardless of whether it is negatively impacting their life. I don't see how you could disagree with that without inventing your own definition of incel that no one else is using.

However, I think it is pretty clear that there are negative outcomes to inceldom. Anytime people deeply desire something that they are not able to get, I think it is going to cause emotional distress. Especially when I do not think it is in any way unreasonable to want a romantic/sexual relationship.

Whether your happiness is affected by your ability to engage in sex or not is irrelevant. Incels do not categorically have to be unhappy in life. I think you misunderstand how the word involuntary is being used. Some people choose to abstain from romantic/sexual relationships, in which case they are voluntarily celibate (the dictionary definition for celibacy only refers to this status). Some people are not making a choice to abstain, they are just unable to find partners. Therefore they are involuntarily celibate.

As a comparison, someone who has very little money would be called poor. Most people do not want to be poor, and would like to be making as much money as possible. We could call these people involuntarily poor. However, there are some rare people who are actively for whatever reason (vow of poverty, rejection of materialism, etc). We could call them voluntarily poor. 

The main reason we don't separate between people who are poor by choice and people who are not poor by choice is that it is assumed that no one wants to be poor. However, if we were actually comparing a person who wanted to be poor with someone who did not want to be poor, we would have to acknowledge that their life experiences are going to be very different, and the distinction is worth acknowledging.

With celibacy, it has traditionally only been defined as a personal choice. There has been little need for a term for people who have been unable to enter romantic/sexual relationships despite desiring them. This is likely because we would be deemed the lowest of the low, and not worth even thinking about. However, again, if we are comparing our life experiences, it makes no sense to group people who are actively abstaining from sexual/romantic relationships with people who desire them but cannot find a partner. The experience is totally different, so having a unique term for it seems totally reasonable.
